relevant_findings: Latex-over-latex is the most common residential repaint scenario with excellent adhesion when surfaces are properly prepared
Existing latex paint typically has lower sheen after years of wear, requiring full recoat to achieve uniform appearance
Wall imperfections become more visible after repaint if not addressed during prep
Freehand cut-in is standard for repaint work; taping is typically reserved for NC or contrasting adjacent surfaces
Two finish coats standard for quality level 4+; single coat acceptable for QL-3 touch-up scenarios
Drying time between coats: 2-4 hours for latex under normal conditions (65-85F, <50% RH)

condition_drivers.description: Adhesion, chalking, peeling, or flaking of existing paint
condition_drivers.impact: Poor condition requires additional prep (scraping, sanding, spot priming)

condition_drivers.description: Nail pops, cracks, dents, scuffs, or texture damage
condition_drivers.impact: Increases repair time; may require skim coating for QL-5

condition_drivers.description: Light-to-dark, dark-to-light, or similar color repaints
condition_drivers.impact: Dramatic color changes may require tinted primer or additional finish coats

condition_drivers.description: Moving from flat to semi-gloss or vice versa
condition_drivers.impact: Higher sheens reveal more imperfections; prep quality must increase

condition_drivers.description: Presence of cabinets, tile, built-ins, or other non-paint assets
condition_drivers.impact: Increases edge work complexity and protection requirements

quality_differences.description: Basic repaint - minimal prep, single finish coat
quality_differences.prep_scope: Light dust/cobweb removal, spot touch repairs only

quality_differences.description: Standard repaint - thorough prep, two finish coats
quality_differences.prep_scope: Full surface clean, fill nail holes/small cracks, light sand repairs

quality_differences.description: Premium repaint - comprehensive prep, two finish coats with inspection
quality_differences.prep_scope: Full clean, repair all imperfections, sand repairs smooth, prime repairs

failure_modes.cause: Painting over contaminated, chalked, or incompatible surface
failure_modes.prevention: Clean thoroughly, test adhesion, spot prime problem areas

failure_modes.cause: Uneven absorption at repairs or inconsistent film build
failure_modes.prevention: Prime all repairs, maintain wet edge, apply uniform coats

failure_modes.cause: Visible difference between cut-in edges and rolled field
failure_modes.prevention: Cut and roll in same session, maintain wet edge, back-roll edges
Work in manageable sections, maintain wet edge, proper loading

failure_modes.cause: Repairs visible through finish due to texture/sheen mismatch
failure_modes.prevention: Match texture, prime repairs, sand smooth before finish

notes_for_materials_manager: Standard interior latex flat/eggshell/satin covers 350-400 SF/gal on smooth drywall
Higher sheen products (semi-gloss) may cover less due to thicker film
3/8" nap roller covers standard for smooth walls; 1/2" for light texture
Brush quality directly impacts cut line quality - premium angular sash recommended for QL-4+
No primer required for latex-over-latex unless repairs present or extreme color change
notes_for_sop_librarian: Prep tasks scale with condition, not just quality level
Edge work (cut-in) is LF-based and separate from field rolling (SF-based)
Repair work should be explicit rounds: REPAIR_R1 (fill), REPAIR_R2 (sand), REPAIR_R3 (prime)
Two-coat finish requires explicit FINISH_R1 and FINISH_R2 tasks
Protection setup/teardown are distinct from painting tasks
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Wall rolling rate: 150-200 SF/hr for single painter depending on obstruction density
Cut-in rate: 100-150 LF/hr for skilled painter
Occupied homes add 15-25% time for protection and careful work
High ceilings (>9') add 10-20% for ladder/scaffold work
Multiple colors in same room multiply edge work significantly

adjacency_notes.strategy: Freehand cut-in; ceiling typically same or similar color in repaint
adjacency_notes.notes: If ceiling being painted in same session, wall cut may be eliminated

adjacency_notes.strategy: Freehand cut-in to baseboard, casing, crown
adjacency_notes.notes: Trim typically contrasting color/sheen; clean cut line essential

adjacency_notes.strategy: Cut-in with extra care; may require tape protection
adjacency_notes.notes: Cabinets, tile, countertops require precision; mask if high-value

assumptions: Existing paint is standard interior latex in acceptable condition
No lead paint or hazardous material concerns
Standard ceiling height (8-10 ft) unless modifier applied
Adequate ventilation and temperature for latex application
Furniture and contents movable or protectable
uncertainties: Exact repair scope unknown until on-site assessment
Color change severity impacts coat count
Asset adjacency complexity varies significantly by room type
